evals.prompt: Use the fleet-model skill. Six instances all have the same broken embedding configuration. Push the fix through them one after another, and stop the whole run if any single one fails. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check. evals.expected_output: The batch rule follows the direction of the transition, not the operator's preference. Broken to attempted-repair continues and reports, because stopping leaves the remaining five broken; good to changed fails fast, because a mixed fleet is described by no rollback. Either way the canary goes first and the run stops there for a separate confirmation.
expectations: The answer says to apply the canary barrier before the remaining instances and to stop for a separate confirmation
The answer says --yes comes only on a later turn after confirmation
The answer names the targets explicitly rather than accepting an empty or fleet-wide selector
The answer mentions fleet.py resolve
